suggested_requirements.text: The migration workflow shall provide an API to handle the migration process and default configuration.
The migration API shall require inclusion of only one header file.
The system shall generate errors in the absence of a provided configuration.
The user shall be able to provide metadata related to the conversion to be stored in the converted files.
The system shall store automatically generated migration metadata in the converted files.
The migration workflow shall be able to call external tools and services.
The migration process shall use persistent, opaque, unique, and global identifiers for records access.
The system shall use an external tool to scan files for malware before conversion.
The API shall allow external tools to be used for file format identification.
The migration process shall be able to run on multiple machines using a messaging infrastructure.
The system shall allow logging to be turned on or off at any time during migration.
The system shall support software checkpoints for managing atomic transactions.
The system shall support a dry-run migration mode to generate reports without writing WARC data.
The system shall detect and report duplicate WARC records based on checksums.
The validation tool shall use metadata in generated WARC files to match records with original ARC files.
The validation tool shall use payload checksum comparisons for core validation.
The validation tool shall support sampling of records for rapid verification.
The validation tool shall support using Heritrix’s arcreader to verify conversion correctness.
The system shall support round-trip validation by migrating WARC files back to ARC and comparing checksums.
The repackaging tool shall filter records based on URL, MIME-Types, size, timestamp, or any WARC field.
The repackaging tool shall support pre and post record, file, and job operations.
The repackaging tool shall include a user-defined metadata record in each repackaged WARC file.
The system shall provide tools to build reports from WARC files.
The system shall export summaries in XML and CSV formats.
The system shall display aggregated WARC summaries in the browser UI.
The system shall display a manifest of WARC files and their locations in the browser UI.
The system shall provide a diff tool to compare WARC sets based on defined criteria.
The system shall provide a tool to draw difference graphs between WARC collections.
The system shall provide a way to view crawl deltas for quality assurance.
The system shall implement server-side rewriting in the WARC browser.
The system shall integrate a proxy mode inside the WARC browser.
The system shall integrate full-text search capabilities with the WARC browser.
The tools shall be able to process a set of multiple WARC files at the same time using explicit naming, wildcard matching, size limitation, or number of items.
The tools shall be able to scale to process large collections using distributed processing and data transport.
The tools shall offer best possible performance to correctly process large collections.
The tools shall be able to run on multiple machines without providing functionality for hardware failure recovery.
The tools shall avoid unnecessary technology dependencies and partner-specific integration technologies.
The tools shall be compliant with Java development environments using web services and RESTful APIs.
The tools shall provide logging facilities to follow command progression.
The tools shall provide easy to adapt shell script wrappers for major commands.
